sources.label: Tycho's own letters: the December 1590 dispatches; to Pontanus, 5 Sept 1595 (TBOO VII)
sources.full: Tycho Brahe, Epistolae astronomicae / Opera Omnia VII: to Thomas Savile 1 Dec 1590 ('nuper Amsterodami cupro insculptae', p.285); to Heinrich Rantzau 7 Dec 1590 (the 'nimiis monilibus onustae' complaint and the re-order, pp.300–301); to Scultetus 8 Dec 1590 (p.302); to Johannes Pontanus 5 Sept 1595 (the Cornelisz print received and criticised, VII:371/373).

sources.label: Friis, Bidrag til dansk Kunsthistorie (1890–1901)
sources.full: F. R. Friis, Bidrag til dansk Kunsthistorie (Copenhagen 1890–1901): the earliest detailed eyewitness description of the Copenhagen pen drawing (p. 222, recording no inscription on it), the Lambert Cornelisz print (p. 228, his reading 'Cornay'), and the painted Mechanica portrait with the Ptolemy and Copernicus statues and the angels' cartouche (p. 238).

sources.label: Mortensen in Rundetaarn 1637–1937 (Copenhagen 1937)
sources.full: Harald Mortensen's chapter in Rundetaarn 1637–1937 (Copenhagen 1937), p. 128, where he lists the Steensgaard picture as the only 'Originalmaleri (?)' of Tycho preserved in Denmark — the position he reversed, without stating new evidence, in his 1946 census; p. 122 reproduces Daniel Hvidt's copy of the panel.

sources.label: Mortensen, 'Portræter af Tycho Brahe' (Cassiopeia, 1946) — the portrait census
sources.full: Harald Mortensen, 'Portræter af Tycho Brahe', Cassiopeia / Tycho Brahe-selskabets årsbok 8 (1946), pp. 54–74 — the baseline census of the lifetime portraits (the painted types, the woodcut, the two de Gheyn engravings, the Cornelisz copy W.1409, the derivatives). Used critically: his 'Goltzius on the verso' claim about the Copenhagen drawing and his 1590 dating of the second engraving are corrected by the 2026 research.

sources.label: Dreyer, Tycho Brahe (1890) — the medal and the life
sources.full: J. L. E. Dreyer, Tycho Brahe: a picture of scientific life and work in the sixteenth century (Edinburgh 1890), ch. 9 and n. 66: the two variants of the 1595 medal, their legends and sizes, a silver specimen in the royal collection at Copenhagen and another at Prague, citing Danske Magazin ii p. 161 and Weistritz ii p. 14.

sources.label: Mortensen, 'Tycho Brahes Bogejermærke' (NTBB XVIII, 1931)
sources.full: Harald Mortensen, 'Tycho Brahes Bogejermærke', Nordisk tidskrift för bok- och biblioteksväsen XVIII (1931), pp. 141–45 — the supralibros dies (the large die reproduced as Fig. 1; the small die's ruff notches, p. 144). Earlier cited in this project as 'Mortensen 1965'; the article is of 1931.

sources.label: Mortensen, 'Fra Tycho Brahes Bogsamling' (Fund og Forskning, 1966)
sources.full: Harald Mortensen, 'Fra Tycho Brahes Bogsamling', Fund og Forskning 13 (1966), pp. 25–32 — the supralibros in two sizes with the medallion mottoes; the Lindenov-gift Calvin/Theocritus volume (the small die's carrier); the three-binding plate p. 29.

sources.label: Van Regteren Altena, Jacques de Gheyn: Three Generations (1983)
sources.full: I. Q. van Regteren Altena, Jacques de Gheyn: Three Generations (The Hague 1983): cat. II 653 (the lost design for the first engraving), 654 (the Copenhagen drawing — 'the design for De Gheyn's second engraving in reverse … traced with a needle for transfer', the 'false monogram HG'), 694 (the Marnix pen model), 677 (the Grotius drawing with Ploos van Amstel's false 'HG 1590'). His c.1595–96 dating of the engravings is corrected at the upper end by the Cornelisz terminus.

sources.label: Statens Museum for Kunst, object record KKSgb5254
sources.full: SMK Open collection record for KKSgb5254 (api.smk.dk): pen and brown ink, 122 × 91 mm; bought 1810 from the heirs of Lorenz Spengler (Lugt 1763); the verso red-chalk 'HG' monogram 'formentlig forfalsket' (presumably forged); attribution history Goltzius → de Gheyn II (Altena) → 'Tilskrevet' Gemperle (the last untenable for the sheet itself — Gemperle died by 1587).

sources.label: Christianson, On Tycho's Island (2000)
sources.full: John Robert Christianson, On Tycho's Island: Tycho Brahe and his Assistants, 1570–1601 (Cambridge, 2000), biographical directory: Jacques de Gheyn II (p.291), Cornelius, Lambert (pp.273–74), Gemperle, Crol. His c.1586–87 dating of the first engraving and the stamp-copies-engraving account are corrected by the letters and the Maestlin keystone.

sources.label: Gigas, 'Nogle Bøger fra Tycho Brahes Bogbinderi' (Bogvennen, 1900)
sources.full: Emil Gigas, 'Nogle Bøger fra Tycho Brahes Bogbinderi', Bogvennen (Copenhagen, 1900) — the earliest detailed description of Tycho's presentation bindings (materials, the two gold ovals + mottoes, the rhombus-and-lily layout, the inside de Gheyn portrait) and twelve KB copies + the foreign copies.

sources.label: 'The Iconography of Tycho Brahe's Small Gilt Brass Quadrant'
sources.full: 'The Iconography of Tycho Brahe's Small Gilt Brass Quadrant', citing Raeder–Strömgren 1946 and Thoren, Lord of Uraniborg.

sources.label: Gassendi, Tychonis Brahei Vita (1655) — the engraved frontispiece
sources.full: Pierre Gassendi, Tychonis Brahei… Vita (The Hague: Vlacq, 1655), frontispiece portrait. See reference/Gassendi_Vita_1654_Reference_Map.md.

sources.label: Beckett & Christensen, Uraniborg og Stjærneborg (1921)
sources.full: Francis Beckett & Charles Christensen, Tyge Brahes Uraniborg og Stjærneborg paa Hven (1921); absorbed at reference/Beckett_Christensen_1921_Uraniborg_Reconstruction.md. Their conjecture that the engraving commission went 'to Goltzius, who passed it to his pupil de Gheyn' is superseded (its premises refuted); their architectural-image genealogy stands.

sources.label: Grinder-Hansen (ed.), Tycho Brahes Verden (Nationalmuseet, 2006)
sources.full: Poul Grinder-Hansen (ed.), Tycho Brahes Verden: Danmark i Europa 1550–1600 (Copenhagen: Nationalmuseet, 2006) — the exhibition volume. An exhibition catalogue rather than a specialist iconography: its captions are the fullest modern account of several of these objects, but it carries identifiable errors (the Gemperlin portrait dated 'formentlig o. 1580'; an astrolabe in the brass-quadrant emblem where Tycho's Latin says a celestial globe and a book; a copperplate 'dated 1586' as the model for the first engraving, of which none is known). Cite it for what it photographs, check it for what it asserts.

sources.label: Tycho Brahe, Epistolae astronomicae (Uraniborg, 1596)
sources.full: Tycho Brahe, Epistolarum astronomicarum libri (Uraniborg, 1596), pp. 243–246 = Opera Omnia VI.273–276 — Tycho's own printed description of the painted decoration of Stjerneborg's warming room, naming all eight astronomers and giving their distichs. A lifetime, first-person, printed source for a lost painting.

sources.label: Mosley, Bearing the Heavens (Cambridge, 2007)
sources.full: Adam Mosley, Bearing the Heavens: Tycho Brahe and the Astronomical Community of the Late Sixteenth Century (Cambridge, 2007), p. 249 — the globe-makers' portraits: Tycho supplied van Langren and Blaeu with impressions of his own engraved portrait, the same image used in the Epistolae, 'to grant legitimacy to the instruments'. The practice begins in 1594, in his lifetime and at his initiative.

sources.label: Karl Madsen, Kunstens Historie i Danmark (c. 1901–07)
sources.full: Karl Madsen, Kunstens Historie i Danmark, pp. 62–64 — the fullest published analysis of the Næsbyholm painted ceiling, identifying the border medallions as the squire's own family and dating the painting to the 1590s rather than to the 1585 building campaign.

sources.label: Vierteljahrsschrift der Astronomischen Gesellschaft 16 (Leipzig, 1881), p. 273
sources.full: The minutes of the Astronomische Gesellschaft's Strasbourg assembly, item 7: 'Herr Safarik vertheilt an die Anwesenden Exemplare einer Photolithographie nach dem einzigen in Prag vorhandenen Originalporträt Tycho Brahe's. Dieses ist ein Aquarell in Folio auf Pergament, einem Exemplar der Astronomiae instauratae progymnasmata vorgebunden, mit autographer Dedication an den böhmischen Magnaten Johann Zajic von Hasenburk, und befindet sich gegenwärtig im Kloster Strahow zu Prag.' Read from the Bayerische Staatsbibliothek's digitisation (shelfmark Astr.u. 209 r-16, urn:nbn:de:bvb:12-bsb11555032-4), printed page 273 = scan 287. Note: the print reads 'befindet sich' (singular); Friis quotes it as 'befinden sich'.

sources.label: Fr. Beckett, Renaissancen og Kunstens Historie i Danmark (1897)
sources.full: Francis Beckett, Renaissancen og Kunstens Historie i Danmark (Copenhagen 1897), pp. 206, 212–13 — the earliest art-historical case for the Gemperlin attribution of the Frederiksborg oil, argued from Jensen's copy against the 1586 engraving and a sketch then under Goltzius's name (derivatives compared to derivatives, never to the signed Vedel 1578 or St Ibb 1578 anchors); records Høyen's 1830 Odense inspection from his Notitsbog.

sources.label: Boldan & Vackářová, Bibliotheca astronomica (2024)
sources.full: Kamil Boldan & Jana Vackářová, Bibliotheca astronomica (Prague: Národní knihovna ČR, 2024), pp. 88–92 — the Strahov-focused Tycho chapter: illustrates the Mechanica presentation copy under its current shelfmark AG XI 56, and returns no trace of the Hasenburk Progymnasmata volume or its watercolour — the strongest and latest of the three independent silences since the 1881 report.

sources.label: Bruun Hansen, 'Da Tycho Brahe gik i kloster' (2013)
sources.full: Gorm Bruun Hansen, 'Da Tycho Brahe gik i kloster — eller et billedes historie', Historisk Årbog for Roskilde Amt (2013), pp. 27–32 — the dedicated study of the Jensen copy at Roskilde Kloster: Høyen's 1830 Odense inspection, the three-stage 1835/1837/1838 removal sequence, and the Schepelern-derived discussion of the picture's descent into the Odense collection. Used critically: its 86 × 69 cm caption figure is a photo-credit carry-over from Tycho Brahes Verden 2006, not an independent measurement.

sources.label: CERL Thesaurus, Lambert Cornelisz (cnp02079345)
sources.full: CERL Thesaurus record cnp02079345 (data.cerl.org/thesaurus/cnp02079345): Lambert Cornelisz, Amsterdam engraver of portraits and title pages, active 1593–1621, with 'Cornely' among the attested name variants (alongside Cornelis/Cornelii/Cornelij/Cornelius) and Jacques de Gheyn II recorded, without date, as his teacher. Spot-check confirmed in the July 2026 dossier run.

sources.label: Christianson, Tycho Brahe and the Measure of the Heavens (2020)
sources.full: John Robert Christianson, Tycho Brahe and the Measure of the Heavens (London: Reaktion, 2020), pp.31–32: the Basel-built quadrant described as a different, larger object (1–1.5 m radius, unstable in wind); the c.1568–69 Basel attribution for the emblem-quadrant of On Tycho's Island Fig. 51 is not repeated — the caption's date is silently dropped.

sources.label: Chytraeus, Variorum in Europa itinerum deliciae (Herborn, 1594)
sources.full: Nathan Chytraeus, Variorum in Europa itinerum deliciae (Herborn, 1594), pp. 596–598 — prints all eight distichs of the Stjerneborg astronomer cycle, including Tychonides, under a heading asserting that the painted icons with gold-lettered distichs exist in the hypocaustum; the preface states the Danish material came largely direct from Tycho. The earliest printed witness to the completed cycle, two years before the Epistolae astronomicae — reporting Tycho's own account, not autopsy. Direct inspection via Internet Archive (variorumineuropa00chyt_0).

sources.label: Tycho Brahe and Prague: Crossroads of European Science (2002)
sources.full: Christianson, Hadravová, Hadrava, Šolc (eds), Tycho Brahe and Prague: Crossroads of European Science (Frankfurt am Main, 2002): Wolfschmidt, p.208 — the destruction account is collective and category-limited (most of the high-accuracy instruments destroyed after 1619, only the two sextants surviving); Fučíková, pp.279–280 — the 1607–1650 Prague Kunstkammer inventories held relatively few astronomical instruments, an anonymous low-valued group of quadrants and sextants, nothing matching this object.

sources.label: Danmarks Adels Aarbog — the Bille-Brahe-Selby genealogy (via finnholbek.dk)
sources.full: Danmarks Adels Aarbog, the Bille-Brahe-Selby genealogy (DAA 1985-87:561-23c and related entries, as transcribed at finnholbek.dk, persons I11378 and I11368) — anchors Hendrik lensgreve Bille-Brahe-Selby's death on 7 May 1938, and establishes that no family member named Preben died in 1938 and none combined 'Baron' with 'Preben'. danmarkshistorien.lex.dk gives the death year as 1937, carried as a flagged minority reading.

sources.label: Danske Magazin II (Copenhagen, 1746) — the medal discussion and plate
sources.full: Danske Magazin, vol. II (Copenhagen, 1746), p. 161 (the engraved plate) and pp. 165–168 (the medal discussion with notes 1–4) — the earliest published account of the 1595 medal. The compilers state that they personally inspected two 'Originaler' (one silver in the Royal Coin Cabinet, one base-metal in Klevenfeldt's collection) and describe specimens as 'afstemplede' (struck); note 4 records the Elephant 'hengende i en Kiæde' on the bust; the editors offer an explicitly unprovable twin conjecture on the occasion (the completion of the star catalogue and the great brass globe reaching usable form in 1595) and float Tycho's nephew Tage Ottesen Tott, then 15–16, as a possible commissioner.

sources.label: Tycho Brahe, De mundi aetherei recentioribus phaenomenis (Uraniborg, 1588)
sources.full: Tycho Brahe, De mundi aetherei recentioribus phaenomenis liber secundus (Uraniborg, 1588) = Opera Omnia IV — the chapter heading 'NOVA MVNDANI SYSTEMATIS HYPOTYPOSIS AB AVTHORE NVPER ADINVENTA', verbatim-verified: the first-person ancestor of the clock plate's third-person banderole 'HYPOTYPOSIS Systematis mundani a Tychone inventi'.

sources.label: Detmold Mechanica, Lippische Landesbibliothek Nl 70.4° (IIIF)
sources.full: Lippische Landesbibliothek Detmold, hand-coloured Astronomiae instauratae mechanica, Nl 70.4°, IIIF manifest digitale-sammlungen.llb-detmold.de/i3f/v20/2547750/manifest — the quadrans minor plate at canvas 2547769 (leaf [16], 4173 × 3223 px), Tycho's Explicatio at canvas 2547770. The only public deep-zoom surrogate of the plate; first-hand inspection (2026-07-20, manifest re-verified 2026-07-21) shows the emblem roundel as uncoloured line-work within an otherwise richly hand-coloured plate, and most of Tycho's verbal programme not legible on the plate.

sources.label: Nationalmuseet, Antikvarisk-Topografisk Arkiv, inv. 572 / DMR-193014 (1860)
sources.full: Nationalmuseet (Copenhagen), Antikvarisk-Topografisk Arkiv, A-sager inv. 572 / DMR-193014, 'Kågeröd kirke. Epitafium over Otte Brahe og Beate Bille', dated 1860, creator Magnus Petersen (samlinger.natmus.dk/dmr/asset/193014) — the only document outside Mortensen 1946 tying Petersen to the epitaph, and it documents him as recorder of its pre-restoration state, not as repainter. Its medium field reads 'photograph' where Mortensen cites a 'Tegning' (drawing), so its identity with the drawing Mortensen cites is unclosed; never inspected at full resolution (6075 × 7415 px, public domain).

sources.label: The arms-supralibros dossier (2026-07-18)
sources.full: research dossier, 'The Brahe coat-of-arms supralibros: the arms oval interrogated on its own terms' (docs/research/2026-07-18-icon-arms-supralibros.md) — the matched-pair adjudication (zero single-oval bindings in ~25–30 examined objects), the 1584 apparatus adjudication, the first independent arms measurement (Stockholm KB De mundi RAR: 106 A, ≈6.6 × 5.3 cm on a transferred scale, medium confidence), and the Bodleian Savile De mundi resolved as a documented negative.

sources.label: Eller, Det nationalhistoriske Museum på Frederiksborg 1878–1978 (1978)
sources.full: Povl Eller, Det nationalhistoriske Museum på Frederiksborg 1878–1978 (Hillerød, 1978), esp. p. 43 — the museum's centennial history: the founding-era history-painting programme (J. C. Jacobsen's foundation, royal decree of 5 April 1878; abandoned c. 1890) and the Stue 27 account of Hansen's 1882 Uraniborg reconstruction, naming Vedel, Queen Sophie and Tycho. A narrative centennial guide, not an inventory catalogue: it names no commissioner, price, or terms for any single canvas, never mentions A 154, and uses no accession-number notation.

sources.label: Rijksmuseum, the genuine Falck engraving of Tycho (RP-P-OB-50.565, 1644)
sources.full: Jeremias Falck, engraved portrait of Tycho Brahe, 1644 (possibly Paris), 309 × 193 mm — a bust in plumed hat within an oval frame, catalogued Block 214 / Hollstein Dutch 214. Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam, RP-P-OB-50.565. Examined at native resolution against the Wellcome photogravure, which matches it on no diagnostic point.

sources.label: Det Nationalhistoriske Museum, Frederiksborg, object record A 155
sources.full: Frederiksborg museum catalogue record inv. A 155 ('Gravsten', maker 'Steffensen', dated 1885–1886, Room 27, person-tagged to Tycho Brahe; frederiksborg.dk) — the structured record never names Prague or the Týn church, but its catalogue photograph shows the exact Týn composition, and the 1937 Rundetaarn jubilee volume independently confirms a Frederiksborg cast; the A 155 = Týn identification is well-supported inference, not documentary.

sources.label: Det Nationalhistoriske Museum på Frederiksborg — published catalogue (frederiksborg.dk)
sources.full: The museum's published online catalogue at frederiksborg.dk, exhaustively enumerated via its four kunstvaerk sitemaps (~1,791 artwork records, July 2026): no Eckersberg drawing and no Christian IV/Tycho sheet; the only Tycho-adjacent holding published is Heinrich Hansen's A 153 (Vedel presenting the ballad collection to Queen Sophie — Christian IV not among the recorded sitters). The museum states institutionally that it owns drawings, prints and photographic portraits that cannot be permanently exhibited for conservation reasons — the published catalogue is a selection, so its negative characterises the publication, not the collection.

sources.label: Friis, Tyge Brahe, en historisk Fremstilling (1871)
sources.full: F. R. Friis, Tyge Brahe, en historisk Fremstilling af hans Liv og videnskabelige Virksomhed (Copenhagen, 1871), p. 298 — the Týn monument raised by the heirs 'nogle Aar senere', after Tycho's wife Kirstine had also found her resting place in the church (1604): the earliest of the three concurring attestations that the erection followed her death, and the source of the record's terminus post quem.

sources.label: Frombork Scientific Inventory — Tycho Brahe: Timepieces
sources.full: 'Scientific Inventory — Tycho Brahe: Timepieces', Nicolaus Copernicus Museum-affiliated inventory (frombork.art.pl), listing 'Clock, 1623, National Museum, Copenhagen (Inv no. D 138)' — the competing unfooted date of 1623 for the console-clock plates, with a description matching the Nationalmuseet record; no source stated. The compiler's use of a genuine Nationalmuseet-derived source is cross-checked on the adjacent D125 entry (the falsely inscribed 'Tycho Brahe 1597' pocket watch) against the museum's own record.

sources.label: Gattei, 'The Engraved Frontispiece of Kepler's Tabulae Rudolphinae' (2009)
sources.full: Stefano Gattei, 'The Engraved Frontispiece of Kepler's Tabulae Rudolphinae (1627): A Preliminary Study', Nuncius XXIV.2 (2009), 341–365 — a panel-by-panel iconographic inventory of the frontispiece. Names Georg Celer (Cöler) of Nuremberg as the engraver, from the plate itself (p. 363); attributes the preliminary sketch (Vienna ÖNB Cod. 9737d, Bl. 30) 'most probably' to Schickard (p. 346); documents the heirs' specification of formal dress and the Elephant regalia (pp. 348, 354). Silent throughout on any de Gheyn model for the Tycho figure — a silence that favours, but does not prove, an independent lineage.

sources.label: Institutional records of the portrait-bearing globes (Frankfurt, Florence, Oxford, Greenwich, New York, London, Rome)
sources.full: Record-level institutional entries for the globe specimens: Deutsche Digitale Bibliothek item GFJOPVOKDRL7SACIADTAQJUDFOFEDQ4P (Historisches Museum Frankfurt, van Langren celestial globe, 1594, inv. X 14 609 — sole survivor of the 1594 Tychonic state; record sourced from Bildarchiv Foto Marburg); Museo Galileo, Florence, inv. 348 (Joan Blaeu, after 1630; catalogue text 'There is a portrait of Tycho Brahe'); History of Science Museum, Oxford, inv. 23709 ('Globes in the Collection' info sheet: 1603 Blaeu; portrait confirmed in the museum's Tycho gallery, mhs.ox.ac.uk/tycho/image23a.html); Royal Museums Greenwich GLB0122 / rmgc-object-19809 (Adriaen Veen with Jodocus Hondius Jr., celestial globe, 1613, 535 mm, 'Below the large constellation of Cetus, on the equator, there is a portrait of Tycho Brahe with text' — posthumous propagation), rmgc-object-19844 (the 1600 Hondius 'globus Tychonicus' GLB0157, no portrait mentioned — corroborated by Stevenson's complete cartouche transcriptions) and GLB0099 / rmgc-object-19786 (the 1589 pre-Tychonic van Langren celestial, positions probably Rudolf Snellius's); Metropolitan Museum objectID 207816 / acc. 1990.84 (Blaeu, after 1621, printed from the 1603 plates per the Met's 1990 Bulletin pp.24–25; portrait presence unconfirmed — open-access photographs show the wrong hemispheres); Science Museum Group co57097 / inv. 1980-1913 (1603 Blaeu, London — distinct from the Oxford specimen; record portrait-silent); Biblioteca Angelica, Rome (1603 Blaeu); Houghton Library, Harvard, *51-2459 PF (Blaeu's first celestial globe, 9 of 12 gores, 'Sphaera Stellifera', ex-Liechtenstein/Hauslab, engraved by Jan Pietersz. Saenredam — call number traceable only to a dead 2009 Houghton blog and the 1952 Liechtenstein finding aid GA195.C35 H7 1952, no live catalogue record).

sources.label: Stevenson, Terrestrial and Celestial Globes (Yale, 1921) — the cartouche transcriptions
sources.full: Edward Luther Stevenson, Terrestrial and Celestial Globes: Their History and Construction, 2 vols. (New Haven: Yale UP for the Hispanic Society of America, 1921; Project Gutenberg 39866/39867, read in full 2026-08-04). Vol. II transcribes the Dutch celestial-globe cartouches: the 1600 Hondius 'globus Tychonicus' (title, Leiden/Franeker dedication, Cassiopeia nova legend — no portrait recorded), the 1601 Hondius 21-cm (figures agreeing with 1600, 'the chief difference lying merely in the matter of size'), the 1603 Blaeu (portrait of Tycho with the motto 'Non haberi, sed esse'), and the 1613 Veen/Hondius Jr. globe's portrait legend 'Effigies Nob. viri Tychonis Brahe Dani Domini de Knudstrup. Summi Mathematici. Aetatis 47.' (verified verbatim) — the frozen age-47 that points the copy-chain back to a 1593/94 model. Vol. I records the van Langren States-General privilege of 9 Sept 1592 renewed 1596 to Jacobus and his sons Arnoldus and Henricus (Stevenson's 'Estates of Amsterdam' for the 1592 grant conflicts with van der Krogt 1984's States-General; prefer van der Krogt). His 1914 Hispanic Society monograph on Blaeu (Gutenberg 75272) adds the Hven data-transactions: Arnold van Langren sent 1591 and refused the incomplete catalogue, Hendrick sent April 1593. Caveat: Stevenson's 'no Blaeu celestial globe earlier than 1602' is superseded by Warner 1971 and van der Krogt 1993 on the Houghton gores.

sources.label: Dekker, 'Globes in Renaissance Europe' (History of Cartography vol. 3) — the census appendix
sources.full: Elly Dekker, 'Globes in Renaissance Europe,' in The History of Cartography, vol. 3 pt. 1 (Chicago UP), with Appendix 6.1, the census of Renaissance globes (chapter PDF at press.uchicago.edu, read and spot-checked verbatim 2026-08-04). Entries verified: no. 130 (van Langren celestial, 1586, 32.5 cm, Linköping Stifts- och Landsbiblioteket), no. 137 (1589, London NMM), no. 148 (1594, Frankfurt Historisches Museum — references Holbrook 1983, 69–73; Van der Krogt 1993, 424–26 and 429; Glasemann 1999, 15–20 — resolving Mosley's '424–426' as pages, not catalogue numbers), no. 161 (celestial gores, Willem Jansz. Blaeu, 1597, 34 cm, Houghton Library — a year against Mosley's 1598, both citing the same van der Krogt pages). The three surviving copies of the van Langren 32.5-cm celestial line documented here supersede Christianson 2000's 'No copy, however, has survived' (pp. 310–311).

sources.label: The van Langren 1594 globe-portrait dossier (2026-08-04)
sources.full: docs/research/2026-08-04-van-langren-1594-globe-portrait-lifetime-census.md — the refresh-and-extend run on this record: the ÆTATIS 47 cartouche read (object-level close read of Mosley fig. 4.7, with the full Effigies tablet, star-count scroll, imprint, and privilege cartouche transcriptions); the withdrawal of the July claim that the miniature 'must descend from v1' (terminus ante quem misread as post quem); the adversarially-adjudicated MEDIUM verdict that the miniature reverses the v2 design; the lifetime globe census (one confirmed portrait globe; Blaeu 1597/98 and Plancius–Hondius 1597/98 indeterminate; Hondius 1600/1601 negative); and the apparatus corrections merged into this record. Supersedes the globes sections of docs/research/2026-07-18-icon-blaeu-globes.md where they conflict.

sources.label: Hannover, Maleren C. W. Eckersberg (1898) — the catalogue raisonné with diary excerpts
sources.full: Emil Hannover, Maleren C. W. Eckersberg: En Studie i dansk Kunsthistorie (Copenhagen, 1898) — the catalogue raisonné, whose diary quotations remain the accessible primary window on the 1831–1842 Christian IV/Tycho series until Villadsen's complete diary edition (2009, undigitised) is consulted: no. 438 (the painting, finished 23 March 1831), no. 441 (the oil sketch, finished 28 April 1831), Raderinger nos. 10–11 (the May–June 1831 etchings), Gengivelser i Træsnit no. 1 (the 18 June 1842 drawing on the block for Flinch's woodcut). Internal page references for nos. 438/441 conflict across retrieval routes — cite by entry number, not page.

sources.label: Horáček, 'Illuminating Methods, Picturing Instruments' (Austrian History Yearbook 52, 2021)
sources.full: Ivana Horáček, 'Illuminating Methods, Picturing Instruments', Austrian History Yearbook 52 (2021), pp. 30–53 — names three instrument images as new 1598 engravings in the Mechanica. Consulted in abstract only; the full text remains paywalled.

sources.label: Ilsøe in Fund og Forskning 44 (2005) — review of Zeeberg's Rantzau bibliography
sources.full: Harald Ilsøe, review of Peter Zeeberg, Heinrich Rantzau: A Bibliography, Fund og Forskning 44 (2005), pp. 498, 505: the three presentation copies of the Res gestae with Rantzau gift-inscriptions dated 15 May 1590 (Manderup Parsberg — later Thore Virgin, Bibliotheca Qvarnforsiana, Uppsala 1946, no. 41, current whereabouts unknown; Christian IV; Duke Hans den Yngre), and the note that Zeeberg's bibliography deliberately excludes the Res gestae as a pure picture series ('ren billedserie').

sources.label: Jern, Uraniborg — herresäte och himlaborg (Lund 1976)
sources.full: Carl Henrik Jern, Uraniborg — herresäte och himlaborg (Lund 1976), p. 139 (printed p. 142) n. 53 — cites Wanscher, Kronborgs Historie (1939), pp. 64–65, for the tapestry figure, but paraphrases him as wearing the Order of the Elephant ('behängd med elefantordén'), the opposite of Wanscher's own argument as quoted verbatim by Mortensen 1946. Cited here for the contradiction, not for the costume.

sources.label: Karlson, Tobias Gemperlin och några skånska 1500-talsporträtt (Lund 1928)
sources.full: William Karlson, Tobias Gemperlin och några skånska 1500-talsporträtt (Lund 1928) — the painter-attribution monograph on Gemperlin and the Danish–Scanian portrait group. Note 24 attests that Hvedholm portraits were transferred to Frederiksborg in 1923 'og erstattedes på Hvedholm af kopier' (and were replaced at Hvedholm by copies) — the mechanism that keeps a 1923 arrival at Frederiksborg live as an alternative route for A 8191. A monograph, not a census: its silence on any Tycho panel is non-diagnostic.

sources.label: Kiel, Schleswig-Holsteinische Landesbibliothek, Yb 54 — LIDO records and IIIF surrogate
sources.full: Schleswig-Holsteinische Landesbibliothek, Kiel: the 16-sheet Res gestae set Yb 54, record-level LIDO catalogue pages (digicult-verbund.de) for Yb 54-1, -2, -15 and -16, and the CC BY-SA 4.0 full-resolution IIIF surrogate of the funeral plate Yb 54-15 (1999 × 1313 px), examined directly in the 18 July 2026 funeral-procession dossier: no numerals and no name-list found on the plate face — only the sheet number '15' and two royal captions. A vision re-check of a higher-resolution surrogate is recommended before treating the negative as final.

sources.label: Kleinschnitzová, 'Ex Bibliotheca Tychoniana' (NTBB 20, 1933)
sources.full: Flora Kleinschnitzová, 'Ex Bibliotheca Tychoniana Collegii Soc. Jesu Pragae ad S. Clementem', Nordisk tidskrift för bok- och biblioteksväsen 20 (1933), pp. 73–97, esp. 81, 85–90 — the six Clementinum own-library volumes (Sign. 8 H 39, 12 H 10, 14 G 30, 14 J 176, 19 C 92, 9 B 135) each carrying 'Porträt- und Wappenstempel in Gold' as a fused pair, and her statement that Tycho used the pair both on dedication gifts and on own-library books he specially valued.

sources.label: Tyge Brahes Meteorologiske Dagbog (la Cour ed., 1876) — the Uraniborg diary
sources.full: Tyge Brahes Meteorologiske Dagbog holdt paa Uraniborg for Aarene 1582–1597, ed. P. la Cour (Copenhagen 1876), pp. 104–107: the entry 'Sepultura Regis' at Frederik II's burial, 5 June 1588, with no travel note for Tycho — against the diary's own convention of logging his journeys off Hven.

sources.label: Lohmeier, Heinrich Rantzau (2000)
sources.full: Dieter Lohmeier, Heinrich Rantzau: Humanismus und Interessenpolitik der Renaissance in Schleswig-Holstein (Heide 2000), pp. 47–49, 76–79: the separate 1588 funeral print series of 21 copperplates by Frans Hogenberg alone, accompanying Rantzau's letterpress Descriptio (Hamburg 1588), as distinct from the 1589 16-plate Res gestae.

sources.label: Marryat, One Year in Sweden I (London, 1862) — the 1860 eyewitness
sources.full: Horace Marryat, One Year in Sweden, vol. I (London: John Murray, 1862), pp. 122–123 and the plate 'Altarpiece of Otto Brahe at Kågeröd' (A. Cooper sc.): visiting in 1860, Marryat records 'of Tycho's scarcely a vestige remains' and pleads for the neglected altarpiece to be restored — attesting the loss of the face before the repaint and fixing the panel as still unrestored at publication. Mortensen 1946 cites the book (as 'I, S. 92' — a slip; the plate faces p. 122) in the same footnote as his repaint sentence, so the two are not independent witnesses to the loss.

sources.label: Tycho Brahe, Astronomiae instauratae mechanica (Wandsbek, 1598)
sources.full: Tycho Brahe, Astronomiae instauratae mechanica (Wandsbek, 1598), TBOO V.56–60: the Fig. 12 equatorial armillary, its pedestal 'e solido et forti ligno', carrying the four icones of Ptolemy, Albategnius, Copernicus 'tum quoque NOSTRAM'; the Fig. 14 great armillary's steel base and portrait-less chapter. English in Raeder, Strömgren & Strömgren, Tycho Brahe's Description of his Instruments and Scientific Work (Copenhagen, 1946), pp. 56–59, 64.

sources.label: Tycho Brahe, Astronomiae instauratae mechanica (Wandsbek, 1598) — the armillary-pedestal portraits
sources.full: Tycho Brahe, Astronomiae instauratae mechanica (Wandsbek, 1598) = Opera Omnia V.58–59; Raeder, Strömgren & Strömgren tr. (Copenhagen, 1946) — Tycho's own description of the great equatorial armillary, whose pedestal carried painted portraits of Ptolemy, al-Battani, Copernicus and Tycho himself, with Copernicus and Tycho in the two visible niches ('those of Copernicus and myself, are seen at d'): a Tycho-authored precedent for the Tycho/Copernicus paired-portrait scheme on decorated instrument surfaces.

sources.label: Tycho Brahe, Astronomiæ Instauratæ Mechanica (1598) — the Quadrans Muralis chapter
sources.full: Tycho Brahe, Astronomiæ Instauratæ Mechanica (Wandsbek 1598), Quadrans Muralis chapter, in the DSL Tekstnet edition (ed. Zeeberg / Gredal Jensen): Tycho's own account of the mural painting — Gemperlin and 'Iohannes de Embdâ Stenwichel' named outright, the landscape hand only as 'Iohannes de Antverpiâ pictor Regius Coronaeburgensis'; his endorsement of the tablet's date ('prout vides') and his praise of the likeness ('vix similior dari possit').

sources.label: Dreyer's Opera Omnia X preface (1923), via Meddelelser fra Ole Rømers Venner (2006)
sources.full: J. L. E. Dreyer's preface to Tychonis Brahe Opera Omnia X (1923), cited via Meddelelser fra Ole Rømers Venner 14/1 (2006), p. 31 (corpus: [internal reference withheld]) — Dreyer's second, unhedged endorsement of the Strahov watercolour as the model for Kilian's plate; like his 1890 endorsement it roots in the single 1881 Šafařík report.

sources.label: Mortensen, 'Tycho Brahe Minder i Prag' (Tycho Brahe-selskabets årsbok, 1942)
sources.full: Harald Mortensen, 'Tycho Brahe Minder i Prag', Tycho Brahe-selskabets årsbok (1942) — records two oil portraits of Tycho at the Prague Observatory as copies after the de Gheyn engravings (Westergaard 1377 and 1394), 'without historical or artistic value', possibly by Pater Klein (director 1732–82); never reconciled with his 1946 account of a Clementinum panel.

sources.label: Mortensen, 'Tycho Brahe Minder i Prag'
sources.full: Harald Mortensen, 'Tycho Brahe Minder i Prag', p. 16 — his own gloss on the Mechanica watercolour exemplars, describing the Stockholm one as the copy belonging to the 'Sv. Vetenskapsakademien': the passage that resolves his 1946 census's 'Royal Library in Stockholm' to the KVA Wargentin copy (same object, loose institutional label).

sources.label: The New Hollstein: The De Gheyn Family, entries 238–239
sources.full: The New Hollstein Dutch & Flemish Etchings, Engravings and Woodcuts, 1450–1700: The De Gheyn Family, entries 238 (the first Tycho engraving) and 239 (the second), with the Introduction on de Gheyn's independent Amsterdam practice from 1588 and the collection lists (pp. 92–95) recording impressions of state I at Amsterdam, Coburg, Dresden, Leiden, London, Rotterdam and Wolfegg, and of state II at Amsterdam, Coburg, Haarlem, London, New York, two Paris collections (one the Fondation Custodia) and Vienna. NH assigns the Epistolae astronomicae use to 239 only.

sources.label: Nielsen, 'Tycho Brahes Bogtrykkeri paa Hveen' (1921) and Dansk Bibliografi
sources.full: Lauritz Nielsen, 'Tycho Brahes Bogtrykkeri paa Hveen' (1921), pp. 181–184 — the bibliographic account of the Orthographia broadsheet (his early-1585 print date is his own hedged inference from the Rantzau dispatch of 1 March 1585, not a printed or physical date) and his verdict that the Marburg sheet is the direct original of the Braun & Hogenberg plate; with his Dansk Bibliografi, entry 432, whose collation tags the Mechanica 'Træsn. og Kobberstik' — woodcuts and copperplates both. Absorbed at reference/Brahe_Bibliography_Nielsen.md.

sources.label: Nielsen, 'Tycho Brahes Bogtrykkeri paa Hveen' (NTBB VIII, 1921)
sources.full: Lauritz Nielsen, 'Tycho Brahes Bogtrykkeri paa Hveen', Nordisk tidskrift för bok- och biblioteksväsen VIII (1921), pp. 182–203 — the Uraniborg press monograph: the 25 Aug 1585 Hagecius letter (Tycho's wood-cutter away in Germany), p. 185 the inference from that letter and undeciphered monograms that German wood-cutters resided at Uraniborg (no cutter is named for any Uraniborg block), p. 196 the woodcut as original, pp. 197–98 the Berlin Sammelband.

sources.label: Nielsen, Dansk Bibliografi 1551–1600, §430
sources.full: Lauritz Nielsen, Dansk Bibliografi 1551–1600 (Copenhagen, 1931–33), §430 (the 1596 Epistolae astronomicae; cf. §432): the collation records 'et kobberstukket Portræt' without naming which engraving — the national bibliography is silent on the state of the inserted portrait. Full-entry transcription in reference/censuses/brahe-mechanica-1598-wandsbek/sources/nielsen_tycho_brahe.txt.

sources.label: Norlind, Tycho Brahe (Lund 1970) — the Mechanica copy census
sources.full: Norlind, Tycho Brahe: en levnadsteckning (Lund 1970), pp. 289–291 — the institution-by-institution census of Mechanica copies transmitting Hasselberg's list; marks the watercolour portrait on exactly four copies (Copenhagen eks. 2 = Hasselberg nr 3, Strahov nr 23 'Med porträtt som i KVA:s', Stockholm KVA nr 1 = Wargentin, Kalocsa nr 22) and records a single Stockholm holding — the basis for resolving Mortensen's 'Royal Library in Stockholm' to the KVA copy. His placement of the KVA portrait 'på titelbladets verso-sida' is carried as possibly precise, possibly loose paraphrase.

sources.label: Norlind's census of the Mechanica
sources.full: W. Norlind, copy census of the Astronomiae instauratae mechanica, which independently anchors the reproductions in Studnička 1901, pp. 44–48, to the Strahov Mechanica presentation copy (today AG XI 56) — the second witness, beside Friis's Addenda, for the surrogate-misidentification caution on the Strahov comparison.

sources.label: Ordbog over det danske Sprog (ordnet.dk/ods)
sources.full: Ordbog over det danske Sprog, s.vv. 'ej' and 'smaa' (ordnet.dk/ods) — the historical dictionary of Danish. Consulted for the dating value of the Levy sheet's orthography: 'ei' is recorded as a deliberate literary archaism from c. 1650 onward, and 'smaae' fluctuates from the eighteenth century, so neither spelling discriminates within the sheet's 1855–1901 bounds. The 'ej' entry was confirmed in the run's citation spot-check; the 'smaa' entry was reached, though its specific reform-date bounds could not be re-verified from the rendered page.

sources.label: Prandtl, Die Bibliothek des Tycho Brahe (1901)
sources.full: Prandtl, Die Bibliothek des Tycho Brahe (1901): reads the nose-prosthesis on Kilian's plate ('Man bemerkt auch hier die Nasen-Prothese') — a feature present in neither de Gheyn state. The reading could not be independently confirmed in the line-work at available resolution and is carried as Prandtl's reading, not as observed fact.

sources.label: Prandtl, 'Die Bibliothek des Tycho Brahe' (Philobiblon V, 1932)
sources.full: Wilhelm Prandtl, 'Die Bibliothek des Tycho Brahe', Philobiblon V (1932), pp. 291–99, 321–29 — the frontispiece plate reproduces his own Gesner Prachtband (Einzelband XXI; now Harry Ransom Center, UT Austin) spread open with gilt ovals on both boards; his list classes it 'Prachtband, Pergament'. Earlier cited in this project under a wrong '(1901)' file label; the article is of 1932.

sources.label: Reindel, 'Bordhimlens dydsmønstre' (Renæssanceforum 2, 2006)
sources.full: Ulrik Reindel, 'Bordhimlens dydsmønstre', Renæssanceforum 2 (2006) — the tapestry-scholarship apparatus: p. 2 nn. 5–6 and 8 (the 15-tapestry survival split per the 1718 Rosenborg inventory, and the 9 Dec 1581 weaving contract, both citing Mackeprang & Christensen 1950); p. 24 nn. 96–97, where the two balustrade noblemen 'identificeres gerne som' Gert Rantzau and Tycho Brahe, citing Honnens de Lichtenberg 1989, p. 152.

sources.label: Resen, Inscriptiones Hafnienses (1668) — the lost Copenhagen picture's inscription
sources.full: Peder Hansen Resen, Inscriptiones Hafnienses, Latinæ, Danicæ et Germanicæ (Copenhagen 1668), pp. 335–336: the full inscription of the lost Copenhagen picture of the aetatis-50 type, recorded from the object then hanging in Frederik III's library — the 'Sub pyramide' motto, the first-person close ('restitutus fui'), the place and date VANDESBECHI AN. MDXCVII, and the signature TYCHO BRAHE OT. Often cited with the year 1663 after Mortensen 1946; the work is of 1668.

sources.label: Rijksmuseum, object record RP-P-OB-9945 (+ correspondence, 31 July 2025)
sources.full: Rijksmuseum object record RP-P-OB-9945 (id.rijksmuseum.nl/200481276): impression of the second engraving, 192 × 138 mm sheet, dated 1593–1597, Public Domain — identified as New Hollstein's illustrated exemplar via the Rijksmuseum's correspondence of 31 July 2025 (Fricke Oosten to C. Westergaard). A second Rijksmuseum impression is RP-P-OB-23.512.

sources.label: Rijksmuseum, object record RP-P-OB-23.512
sources.full: Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam, RP-P-OB-23.512 — the reference impression of the signed state: the museum's record names Jacob van Meurs I as printmaker after an original print by Jacques de Gheyn II, ties the sheet to the second edition of Gassendi's Vita (The Hague: Vlacq, 1655), and cross-references New Hollstein Dutch 239 copy b; the sheet itself is dated only 1630–1680. The signature 'I.v.Meurs. Scul.' read letter-exact on the full-resolution CC0 scan. https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en/collection/RP-P-OB-23.512

sources.label: Segonds, 'A propos d'un emblème de Tycho Brahe' (1994) — cited, unread
sources.full: Alain Segonds, 'A propos d'un emblème de Tycho Brahe dans les Mechanica', in W. D. Hackmann and A. J. Turner (eds), Learning, Language and Invention: Essays presented to Francis Maddison (Aldershot & Paris: Variorum / Société Internationale de l'Astrolabe, 1994), pp.261–272 — the one earlier dedicated study of the emblem, treating a possible relationship to Rollenhagen's Nucleus emblematum and the motto's genealogy. Citation verified; the primary text remains UNREAD (documented null, 2026-07-18) — everything known of its argument is mediated through Perkins & Taub 2015.

sources.label: Simonsson, Kågeröd kyrka: kulturhistorisk karaktäristik och bedömning (2015)
sources.full: Kristina Simonsson, Kågeröd kyrka: Kulturhistorisk karaktäristik och bedömning (JAIS arkitekter AB for Svenska kyrkan, Lunds stift, 2015) — the certified heritage assessment of the church: the epitaph placed in front of the blocked south portal (former vapenhus entrance) in the 1914 Wåhlin renovation, and the registry handles (Bebyggelseregistret anläggnings-ID 21300000008127, byggnad 21400000548881, fastighet Svalöv Kågeröd 18:1). The 1914 placement is independently carried by the Bebyggelseregistret byggnad record.

sources.label: Statens Museum for Kunst, Eckersberg object records (KKS2591, KKSgb5837, KKSgb5834)
sources.full: SMK Open collection records (api.smk.dk) for Eckersberg's Christian IV/Tycho subject: KKS2591 (the first etching, contemporary pencil inscription dating it May 1831; acquired 1898), KKSgb5837 (the reworked second etching, published by the Kunstforeningen; SMK's curatorial note derives it after the painting), and KKSgb5834 (the 1837 Tycho/Rømer cover etching for Ursin). Exactly three Eckersberg objects on the subject, all etchings, zero drawings — the SMK leg of the triple negative on the 2006 sheet.

sources.label: Studnička, Prager Tychoniana (1901)
sources.full: F. J. Studnička, Prager Tychoniana (Prague: Verlag der kön. böhm. Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften, 1901) — the Strahov-era survey of Prague Tycho relics, read in the German original with full house translation: p. 60 and the item C.I footnote, which borrows an illustration from a Progymnasmata, 1603, at Strahov, proving a copy was accessible to him in 1900–01. Its printed wrapper carries the reproduction of the standing-Tycho watercolour used as this record's plate; the catalogue itself is silent on the Hasenburk Progymnasmata volume and the 1881 episode.

sources.label: Tychonis Brahe Opera Omnia — the quadrant's primary witnesses
sources.full: Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia (ed. Dreyer): V, 12–15, the Mechanica's quadrans minor chapter with Tycho's own description of the emblem ('Juvenis laurea insignitus', celestial globe and book); VI, 284–285, the 1591 instrument synopsis for Landgrave Wilhelm IV of Hessen-Kassel, item XXV — the earliest dated witness to the emblem's description, motto included; X, 38–39, the December 1573 eclipse log cited by Thoren as the dating anchor.

sources.label: Tychonis Brahe Opera Omnia IX (Dreyer ed.)
sources.full: Tychonis Brahe Dani Opera Omnia, ed. J. L. E. Dreyer, vol. IX, pp. 175–78 — the press motto and the effigies and arms distichs printed under CIRCA EFFIGIEM TYCHONIS / CIRCA ARMA TYCHONIS, with the trailing apparatus note sourcing them from an exemplar printed by Tycho's own press, 'Uraniburgi 1584' (cf. Cod. Vindob. lat. 10686/7); Dreyer's note-after-item convention adjudicated from the surrounding pages.

sources.label: Thoren, The Lord of Uraniborg (1990)
sources.full: Victor E. Thoren, The Lord of Uraniborg: A Biography of Tycho Brahe (Cambridge, 1990), pp.75–78, 151 n.17, 163 n.39: the dating anchor for the small gilt quadrant — Tycho's log of the lunar eclipse of 8 December 1573 (TBOO X, 38–39) contains an unambiguous reference to this instrument, deployed against Dreyer's post-1576 Uraniborg claim; the emblem's programme linked to the Urania elegy of spring 1573; the instrument obsolete by c.1580 and never used again; the 'Q. min.' abbreviation in the observation logs denotes the Quadrans mediocris, not this instrument.

sources.label: The 'Typus Pompae Funebris' catalogue records (BnF; British Museum)
sources.full: BnF catalogue général, ark:/12148/cb32491664b — 'Typus pompae funebris 5. Junii anno 1588…', a folio prepared by Heinrich Rantzau and dedicated to Christian IV (record fetched directly); British Museum P_1870-0514-2874 — 'Typus Pompae Funebris', a 1588 print (surfaced via search snippet only, direct fetch refused; needs re-verification). Together they establish 'Typus Pompae Funebris' as a genuine period title.

sources.label: Vellev, 'Et industrianlæg og en votivsten på Hven …' (Renæssanceforum 12, 2017)
sources.full: Jens Vellev, 'Et industrianlæg og en votivsten på Hven …', Renæssanceforum 12 (2017) — peer-reviewed account of the Hven votive stone, whose paired Brahe (paternal) and Bille (maternal) arms independently confirm the blazon of the plain paternal shield, sable, a pale argent, carried alone on the supralibros.

sources.label: Gassendi, Tychonis Brahei Vita (Paris 1654) — the unsigned state
sources.full: Pierre Gassendi, Tychonis Brahei… Vita (Paris: Vidua Mathurini Dupuis, 1654), the first edition, with the portrait bound facing Book One. Collated impressions: Royal Danish Library 42,-243 and BnF RES-M-580 (via Gallica) — caption word-for-word and line-break-identical with the 1655 impression, including the DISPOSITORVM variant, but unsigned; BnF's iconographic notice (cote 2757A) catalogues the 1654 engraver as 'Non identifié'.

sources.label: Wellcome Collection catalogue, the photogravure sheet (1355i / V0000746)
sources.full: Wellcome Collection, London, catalogue record atbe9xn8 (no. 1355i / image V0000746): 'Tycho Brahe. Photogravure after J. Falck', citing R. Burgess, Portraits of Doctors & Scientists in the Wellcome Institute (1973), no. 405.7. Plate number 8279; IIIF native maximum 2200 × 3190 px; Public Domain Mark. The 'after J. Falck' title takes the sheet's lettering at face value; Burgess's entry itself remains unexamined.

sources.label: Fortegnelse over indbo fra Steensgaard (V. Winkel & Magnussen, 1938) — the dispersal catalogue
sources.full: Fortegnelse over indbo fra Steensgaard (Copenhagen: V. Winkel & Magnussen, auction Thursday 20 October 1938, 48 pp.) — the sale that dispersed the Steensgaard contents after Hendrik lensgreve Bille-Brahe-Selby's death. Known so far only through a bookseller's listing (Gurra's Books, Hemse, item #026711): a located lead, not yet an examined anchor — the listing's title-page transcription names the decedent 'Baron Preben Bille-Brahe-Selby', conflicting on both forename and title with the documented Hendrik lensgreve; most likely a transcription error, but unresolved until the physical title page is seen.

sources.label: Zeeberg, Den praktiske muse (1993)
sources.full: Peter Zeeberg, Den praktiske muse (1993), pp. 18–21 with n.19 — reads the Tychonides figure as a 'tænkte arvtager' (notional heir), printing »Tychonides« in scare quotes; absorbed at reference/Zeeberg_1993_Praktiske_Muse_Reference_Map.md.

sources.label: Blaeu, Grooten Atlas (1664) - the Hven instrument plates
sources.full: Joan Blaeu, Grooten Atlas, oft Werelt-beschryving (Amsterdam 1664), the Hven/Uraniborg section: the copper re-engravings of the Mechanica instrument figures with Dutch text, incl. BOTH small equatorial armillaries (the steel-braced one, and the portrait-pedestal one under 'Armillae S') and the mural-quadrant interior. Examined in the Utrecht University exemplar (D:/Digital surrogates/utrecht-ac62-rariora, images 187-222); the portrait-armillary plate is archived at plates/icon-armillary-pedestal-blaeu1664.jpg.

sources.label: TBOO X - the 1582-85 observation protocols (construction anchor)
sources.full: Tychonis Brahe Opera Omnia X (Dreyer ed.): the observational diaries 1582-85. The dated 'per Armillas' entry in the Oct-Nov 1584 Jupiter/Aldebaran series (printed p. 321; corpus vision re-OCR opera_10_p0363.txt, verified 2026-08-04) plus Thoren's citations X, 292 and 363 anchor the portrait armillary's construction to summer 1584 (tested 20 August 1584 per Christianson 2020, pp. 126-127).

sources.label: Icones instrumentorum (Uraniborg 1596, Nielsen 975) - the block's first issue
sources.full: Icones instrumentorum quorundam astronomiae instaurandae gratia a Tychone Brahe Dano...elaboratorum (Uraniborg, [1596]): 18 letterpress-free woodcut pulls of the instrument blocks, issued as a supplement with some copies of the 1596 Epistolae astronomicae; presentation copies to Christian IV and Chancellor Friis December 1596 (Norlind p. 235; Mosley App. I; Dreyer p. 230 n.2). The armillary leaf prints the Fig. 12 block with the full portrait pedestal - examined in the Stockholm KB exemplar (D:/Digital surrogates/brahe/brahe-icones-1596-stockholm-kb.pdf) 2026-08-04, same-block verdict on total-design + letter-key correspondence. Census: reference/censuses/brahe-icones-1596/ (4 copies incl. Sophia stock 5766). Dossier: docs/research/2026-08-04-icones-instrumentorum-1596-block-dating.md.

rejected.object: The Næsbyholm painted ceiling — border medallions
rejected.claim: Implied to contain a portrait of Tycho by inclusion in a Tycho volume.
rejected.verdict: Rejected. No source has ever proposed any head as Tycho.
rejected.basis: Karl Madsen, Kunstens Historie i Danmark, pp. 62–64: 'Medaillonportræterne er sikkert for største Delen Portræter af Herremanden og hans Familie' — the squire being Steen Brahe, Tycho's brother. Absent from Mortensen, Dreyer, Friis, Norlind, Christianson, Beckett & Christensen and Studnička alike. Its presence in the 2006 book is a social-history illustration choice. The ceiling itself is at Nationalmuseet.

rejected.object: The Kunstkammer ivory box with portrait medallions
rejected.claim: An 18th-century Kunstkammer tradition held that the two medallions showed Tycho Brahe and his wife.
rejected.verdict: Rejected — but on an undefended argument.
rejected.basis: Grinder-Hansen 2006: 'det hele er en skrøne' — the whole thing is a fable — because the man's head 'har ikke den fjerneste lighed med kendte portrætter af Tycho Brahe'. That is iconographic comparison without stated working: he names no compared portraits and shows no reasoning. The rejection is very probably right, and is recorded here as a rejection rather than as a demonstration. The object itself is untraced.

rejected.object: Langhans's photographs of the skull and upper body, Prague 1901
rejected.claim: Sometimes treated as images of Tycho.
rejected.verdict: Out of scope, not false. These are documentary photographs of physical remains, not made likenesses.
rejected.basis: Mortensen's census correctly ends at the Týn effigy, and the 2006 volume files them in a burial chapter, not a portrait chapter. Two things worth carrying: they falsify the claim, still circulating, that no photographic record survives from 1901; and the 'Det Kongelige Bibliotek' line under them is a reproduction credit, not a statement of ownership — no holding record for either photograph has been found.

rejected.object: 'Tycho Brahe's chair' and the other Kunstkammer relics
rejected.claim: Objects associated with Tycho by 18th-century tradition.
rejected.verdict: Rejected. The chair is a Norwegian peasant chair.
rejected.basis: Grinder-Hansen 2006, recording the Kunstkammer protocol of 1737 which enters a hollowed-trunk 'knubstol' as Tycho's chair from Uraniborg. Included here because the same appetite that produced the chair produced the ivory box: an 18th century that wanted Tycho relics and found them.
